record.original_question: Consider the continuous high-low guessing framework restricted to two guesses, with payoff (g2-h)^2 to the hider. What are the optimal strategies in this two-guess quadratic-payoff game?

evidence.quote: Instead of ∑ |g n −h| one may also consider other norms or other payoffs. Tom Ferguson has studied a game with two guesses only, in which the payoff to the hider is (g2 −h)2. Despite its apparent simplicity, this game is non-trivial and the optimal strategies are not easy to ﬁnd, see [6].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-person zero-sum game played as follows. A hider secretly chooses a real number h in [0,1] according to some probability distribution. A searcher, without knowing h, chooses two real numbers g_1, g_2 in [0,1] (the "guesses"), where g_2 may depend on information revealed after the first guess in the standard continuous high-low fashion: after the searcher announces g_1, the hider truthfully reveals whether h < g_1, h = g_1, or h > g_1, and then the searcher selects g_2. The payoff from the searcher to the hider is

    (g_2 − h)^2.

The searcher wants to minimize, and the hider wants to maximize, the expected payoff. Determine the value of this game and describe an optimal (possibly mixed) strategy for the hider and an optimal strategy for the searcher.
artifact.status_search_result: A brief web search located Ferguson's game theory writings on guessing/high–low games but did not surface a definitive published solution to the specific two-guess continuous variant with quadratic payoff (g_2 − h)^2. The problem is described in the literature as nontrivial with optimal strategies not easy to find; no conclusive evidence of a complete solution was found.

status_evidence.title: GAME THEORY — Thomas S. Ferguson
status_evidence.snippet: Ferguson's game theory text discusses guessing and number-hiding games and optimal mixed strategies, but a complete solution to the quadratic two-guess variant is not located.
status_evidence.claim: No conclusive solution to the specific two-guess quadratic-payoff high-low game was located in available sources.
